Because the gold fact is a compound statement, only part is captured; as written the full gold item is not entirely represented, so marked omitted.

Gold: passing urine okay. Generated HPI-008: passing urine normally. Matches.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold CC is cough and cold without duration; generated CC adds 5 days duration and describes constant rhinorrhea. Conceptually related but adds detail not present in gold and changes phrasing; no direct supporting gold fact for this exact statement.

Gold confirms dry cough and duration but does not specify frequency 'every 20–30 minutes'. The presence of dry cough is supported (hpi-002), but the detailed frequency is an addition; no gold text supports that specific rate.

Gold: feels hot, hasn't measured temperature (hpi-003), but does not mention alternating chills. 'Intermittent subjective fevers' and 'no thermometer reading' align with gold; 'alternates with chills' is an added detail. Composite fact thus includes additions; partially supported by hpi-003 but not entirely.

Gold ROS specifies a different negative list: no sputum/hemoptysis, no epistaxis/sinus pain, no SOB/inspiratory pain/wheeze, no vomiting, etc. Generated HPI-007 denies chest pain, SOB, hemoptysis, vomiting, current diarrhea, rashes, headache, visual changes. Some overlap (SOB, hemoptysis, vomiting) but chest pain, rash, headache, visual changes, and 'current diarrhea' are not in gold; inspiratory pain, wheeze, epistaxis/sinus pain, weight loss, thirst, urinary frequency are not included here. Overall this is a broader negative ROS not specifically supported by gold.
Gold facts contain no information on allergies. A statement of 'no known medication allergies' is new and unsupported in gold.
Intermittent hay fever/allergic rhinitis is not mentioned anywhere in gold. Pure addition.
Generated: smoking status not documented / patient did not answer. Gold: patient is a non-smoker (sh-001). Direct conflict.
Generated: no vital signs were documented. Gold physical findings include height and weight. Claiming no vitals at all contradicts existing anthropometric data (even if not full vitals like BP).
Generated: no physical exam was documented. Gold has physical findings of height and weight, indicating at least some physical data. This is inconsistent.
Generated: positive for green rhinorrhea. Gold HPI describes runny nose but not color; ROS in gold does not record rhinorrhea. The 'green' detail and its placement under ROS are additions.

Negative for ear pain is not in gold facts. Added ROS detail.
Negative for sore throat is not documented in gold ROS. Addition.
Negative for rash is not mentioned in gold. Addition.

Instruction to obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature at home is not in the gold plan. Gold only says check fever with thermometer within the follow-up context but not as a discrete plan item; this generated framing and emphasis are additional.
Gold plan does not mention considering antibiotics if not settling/fever persists; only follow-up triggers are described (contact us, monitor). Antibiotic consideration is new.

Several elements—obtain thermometer, maintain fluids and rest, use cough suppressant only at night—extend beyond the explicit gold plan, which only mentions Lemsip and cough syrup timing and course expectation. Fluids/rest and thermometer acquisition are additions.
Gold lists Metformin as a current med but does not mention confirming dose/route/frequency with primary care. This verification step is additional care-planning detail.
Gold lists Lisinopril but does not instruct to confirm dose/BP control or note that a reported dose is likely incorrect. Added plan-level and uncertainty details.
Managing at home with symptomatic care and no new prescriptions is not explicitly stated in gold. It is consistent but not documented there.

Gold follow-up: contact if symptoms worsen, fever persists, specific red flags (phlegm, blood in sputum, nose bleeds). Generated FU-001 is a more generic 'reassess if symptoms worsen or do not improve' without those exact red flags. Concept overlaps but wording and scope are different; considered an addition rather than strictly supported by a specific gold fact.

Generated lists detailed thresholds: fever >37.5–38°C, worsening cough, new sputum production, hemoptysis, SOB, chest pain. Gold mentions fever persisting, coughing up phlegm, blood in sputum, nose bleeds. Some overlap (fever persistence, phlegm, blood in sputum), but temperature thresholds, SOB, chest pain, and lack of nose bleeds differ. Overall this is an expanded and partly divergent red-flag set, best classified as addition.
Gold does not specify 7–14 days for symptom persistence before follow-up; it only advises to contact if symptoms worsen or fever persists. The 7–14 day timeframe is new.
